Types of Pregnancies

The journey to motherhood is one marred with expectations and anxiety. It is a moment of high hopes and anticipated joy. On the extreme side, however, it is quite unfortunate that not all mothers get the chance to hold their â€˜bundle of joyâ€™ at delivery. Some pregnancies just donâ€™t happen right, leading to miscarriage, while others have to be terminated in their early stages. Some of the factors contributing to the different types of pregnancies include, multiple eggs/sperm during fertilization, differences in hormones and reproductive systems in women, and underlying health conditions, among others.

 

At times, it is hard to understand the happenings around pregnancy, or even the risk factors that come in handy when one is pregnant. It is always advisable to seek a specialist to walk with you during your pregnancy to ensure your baby is growing right and mitigate risks of complications. As it is not always that pregnancies go right, knowing the different types of pregnancies and the circumstances under which they happen can help address individual scenarios and, with the help of a specialist, increase the chances of survival in troubled pregnancies. Below are some of the most common types of pregnancies you are likely to hear of.

Types of Pregnancies

1. Intrauterine pregnancy

Intrauterine pregnancy is the ideal form of pregnancy, whereby the fertilized egg gets implanted inside the uterus and develop normally.

 

2.Ectopic pregnancy

Ectopic pregnancy occurs when the fertilized egg implants outside the uterus. A most common form of ectopic pregnancy is the tubal pregnancy, where implantation occurs in the fallopian tube instead of the uterus. Ectopic pregnancies are not viable, and in the case a miscarriage does not happen, the pregnancy has to be terminated.

 

3.Molar pregnancy

A molar pregnancy happens in two forms: complete and partial, where the embryo and the placenta develop abnormally and may result in a tumor. The pregnancy ends up in miscarriage, or an abortion may be initiated as it is not viable.

 

4.Lupus pregnancy

This is a type of pregnancy common in women with lupus disease. Itâ€™s a high-risk pregnancy that demands the intervention of a health specialist.

 

5.Chemical pregnancy

While most pregnancies are detectable through an ultrasound, a chemical pregnancy is not detectable and is lost almost immediately after implantation.

 

6.High-risk pregnancy

Most high-risk pregnancies are common in women around and above the age of 35 years, those with underlying health conditions or cases of multiple fetuses, and, at times, prior childbirth complications.

 

7.Singlet pregnancy

A Singlet pregnancy is a normal and viable pregnancy. It occurs where a single egg is fertilized by a single sperm and one fetus develops thereof.

 

8.Multiple pregnancy

Unlike a Singlet pregnancy, multiple pregnancy happens when one fertilized egg splits resulting into two or more embryos, or two different eggs are fertilized by two different sperms forming twin babies.

 

9.Breech pregnancy

In a scenario where the fetus has the head positioned at the upper side of the uterus contrary to normal pregnancies where the head faces downwards/ birth canal ready for delivery such, is known as breech pregnancy.

 

As evidenced above, not all pregnancies go as smoothly as every mother would wish for. Walking the journey to the end and giving birth to a healthy baby is by far a miracle and a gift. blog_posts.title: Should You Be Eating for Two When Pregnant?
blog_posts.content:
We know there are days you feel so hungry while pregnant, and you can eat like a horse. Considering the belief that you should be eating for two, it doesnâ€™t seem a bad idea to devour as much food as you can.

But the truth is that eating for two during pregnancy is false. Whatever you eat during your pregnancy affects your well-being and your babyâ€™s development. So, paying attention to your eating habits is more important than ever.

Read on to learn if you should eat for two while pregnant.

Eating Right When Pregnant

Well, itâ€™s not a myth that you should eat for two while pregnant, thanks to your bodyâ€™s increasing need for nutrition and calories. But your body doesnâ€™t need double the nutrients or the extra calories.

Interestingly, you donâ€™t require additional calories during the first trimester. You only need an extra 300 calories in the second and third trimesters. With this in mind, you can see that you donâ€™t have to eat for two.

Besides, overeating during pregnancy is a recipe for disaster, and it leads to:

Weight gain, which may be challenging to shed it off after giving birth

It makes you vulnerable to high blood pressure and can result in preeclampsia

Increases the likelihood of gestational diabetes

However, there are exceptions to these caloric requirements, especially if youâ€™re significantly underweight and you probably need more calories or when youâ€™re overweight and need to reduce the calories. So be sure to check with your doctor to advise you on your daily caloric needs.

How to Meet Your Caloric Demands in Pregnancy

Now that you know you donâ€™t need to eat for two, the best way to ensure you get the right calories is not by monitoring your every bite. Instead, increase your intake of nutrient-dense food that meets your caloric demand while keeping up with your prenatal visits so your doctor can keep tabs on your weight.

Donâ€™t worry if youâ€™re not gaining the weight as required or gaining it too fast. Hereâ€™s what to do to put you back on track:

If youâ€™re gaining too much weight quickly, you consume more calories than you need. With the help of your doctor, you can adjust your diet. Cut back on calorie-dense, processed foods with less nutritional value. Double up on the essential minerals and vitamins for your babyâ€™s development.

If youâ€™ve hit your second trimester and are not gaining weight because of food aversions, youâ€™re not meeting your nutritional needs. Include high protein foods, healthy fats like seeds, nuts, whole dairy, and salmon. Also, talk to your doctor if you still have challenges gaining enough weight.

In Closing

You shouldnâ€™t eat for two while pregnant since your caloric needs donâ€™t change in the first trimester and only increases by 300 calories towards the end of the pregnancy. You can meet your caloric and nutrient needs by following a healthy diet. Remember to consult your doctor for the ideal weight gain in your pregnancy.

blog_posts.title: Healthy Ways to Conquer Pregnancy Cravings
blog_posts.content:
Pregnancy cravings can be explained by the extra need for strength and energy needed as the baby grows. Though not all women get to experience it, it is normal and common with pregnant mothers. What makes the cravings a topic for discussion is how weird and unhealthy some of these cravings can be. From craving for dirt, ice creams, dust, and petrol, among others, yielding to these cravings can have irreversible and damaging effects and thus need to be kept in check.

Pregnancy Cravings

Below are some tips to help you avoid giving in to unhealthy pregnancy cravings.

Mindful feeding

One major concern with pregnancy cravings is the unprecedented weight gain due to overeating or excessive snacking. Getting yourself back to your desired weight and body figure after giving birth can be quite a tussle if you do not keep your appetite in check during pregnancy. It is always advisable to maintain a healthy diet for the sake of your health and that of your baby. Plan your meals beforehand, and if itâ€™s a must, plan for your snacks so you do not end up rummaging for the wrong ones. It is at this time you will need to avoid sugary foods and drinks at all costs.

 

Do not skip meals

What causes the frequent urge to eat is the need for the body to acquire much-needed energy. One sure way to reduce cravings is by making sure you are not hungry. It is advisable to take your meals in the right proportions at the right time. Skipped meals create a window for cravings and before you know it, you are right deep into junk foods.

 

Keep your body hydrated

Most people will avoid drinking water during pregnancy for fear of having to pee all the time. As uncomfortable as it may be, your body needs the drink for proper hydration. Taking water before meals also helps you get full faster and consequently, reducing the risk of overeating. Water also helps with delayed gratification whereby you do not have to eat when you get the urge to. Drinking water in place of food will keep you longer before your next meal.

 

Prenatal supplements

Some of the weirdest cravings include craving for dust or dirt. In most cases, pregnant women run for soil or baked clay. However, did you know that you can avoid altogether? In actual sense, what your body lacks is some form of minerals such as iron and calcium. Taking a healthy diet rich in these minerals will shoo away cravings. In a case where the healthy diet requirement is not met, daily prenatal supplements can be helpful. With prenatal supplements, you do not have to worry about your baby missing out on vital nutrients, and this way, you can have your healthy meals without yielding to unhealthy cravings that could be harmful to you and the baby.

 

You do not have to bear the guilt of feeding your cravings at the expense of your health. As difficult as it is, it is not impossible. Did you know that to some extent, it is all in the head, and distracting your mind not to think about food can also work? Outdoor activities such as walks can help you keep your mind engaged.

blog_posts.title: Why Sleep Training Is Important For Your Baby
blog_posts.content:
Sleep Training is a very important aspect for a baby in their growth especially in their first few months and as moms it is important to understand the importance of sleep training.

As a mom, what would you term as the most stressful experience with your baby? Well, most moms, if not all, will agree that getting their little ones to sleep is quite a tussle. Almost every mom can narrate an instance they have had to tiptoe to the door only to turn and find the baby staring back, wide awake. Worse still is when your baby wonâ€™t sleep until after hours of rocking them in your arms only to tuck them in and you find them staring back.

Wait, are we forgetting the midnight yells? In other words, knowing exactly how and when to put your baby to sleep is a thumbs-up for many reasons. Sleep-deprived kids are mostly irritable and dull, which are some of the reasons why you should be concerned about how much sleep your baby gets. Outlined below are some benefits of sleep training on your baby.

Sleep Training Establishes a Routine

A sleep schedule is essential in ensuring your kid gets enough sleep. It is wise to have your kid stick to a strict sleep schedule for daytime naps and bedtime at night.

Sleep Training Reduces nighttime waking

 Sleep-trained babies get uninterrupted sleep with fewer waking from time to time, which is healthy for both the mother and the baby. With fewer distractions, you can get quality sleep and rest, giving you enough energy to care for your baby.

Helps with self-soothing: it is easy for a sleep-trained baby to fall asleep independently and stay asleep longer. Sleep training creates a sense of independence, relieving you as a parent the hustle of soothing your baby to sleep, which may be tedious and unsuccessful sometimes.

Improves daytime behavior: Sleep-deprived babies tend to be irritable and cranky, which explains the untold crying and restlessness just before they fall asleep. With sleep training, restlessness is avoidable as your baby is tuned to a specific sleep pattern, which comes naturally over time. With enough sleep, your baby will be more lively and at ease.

Supports cognitive development: Sleep is necessary for brain development. Sleep training helps develop discipline when it comes to sleep routines. A sleep-trained baby gets quality sleep as opposed to an untrained baby. Enough sleep encourages brain development, which is an essential aspect of growth for your baby.

Encourages healthy sleep habits: Sleep training helps kids develop good sleeping habits, which are helpful even in their upper years. It becomes easy for your baby to fall asleep naturally without soothers or swaddles. You wonâ€™t have to worry about moving your baby into their own bed, as sleep training helps them become independent.

 

Sleep training is essential for your baby as it helps develop good sleeping habits with less waking up at night. It also helps with cognitive development and the general growth of your baby. However, sleep training is not easy to achieve without patience and consistency.

blog_posts.content:
Nairobi families expecting a new bundle of joy, commemorate this magical time with a stunning family pregnancy photo shoot in Kenya at Fiesta House Attire.

Best explained, mommy wars are differences that bring about a lack of consensus on whatâ€™s best when it comes to parenting. There will always be a mom out there who thinks your parenting is wanting and that they have the best opinion of what should and should not be done. In most cases, however, mommy wars start at an individual level _ the inner voices that question the sanity of your parenting decisions. The noise may be so much that you cannot focus on the task at hand _ being a mom. This article seeks to explore some common mommy wars and, while at it, discuss tips on how to stay focused amidst them, especially as a new mom.

 

Common Mommy Wars

1. Weaning your baby vs exclusive breastfeeding

2. A working mom vs a stay-at-home mom

3. Daycare for your baby vs nanny care

4. Differences on how to discipline your kid, among other differing takes

 

How to stay focused

Make peace with your choices. One sure way to maintain focus is by ensuring you are at peace with your choices. For instance, if you choose to be a stay-at-home mom for the benefit of your baby, it should not worry you that other moms are working.

 

Avoid judging. As the saying goes, judge not rest you get judged. Most of the mommy wars are a result of judging and counter-judging. Every criticism of how a fellow mom goes about her parenting will most likely be met with a counter-criticism, creating a trail of never-ending judging competition. Appreciating the fact that how you take charge of things in your home may not always sync with what other moms do and that it is completely fine will do you so much good.

 

Concern yourself less with what others are doing. Unless you are seeking support or ideas, do not concern yourself with what happens around you all the time. Limit yourself to interactions that grow you without caring what opinions there are. Likewise, do not let the opinion of others get to you if you do not buy it.

 

Limit your exposure to social media. Social media is important for updates and news on what is going on. Moderation is, however, needed as not everything is as real as it seems. Social media platforms act as catalysts for most mommy wars. It is good to understand that not everything on those platforms is white and black as it seems.

 

Finally, seek support. Engaging with like-minded mothers can do you a lot of good in your parenting journey. Surrounding yourself with moms who share your way of thinking will limit your exposure to baseless arguments and criticism, and that is all the peace you need - the assurance that somebody else sees things from your angle and that there is nothing wrong in following what you believe in.

 

Different opinions on how to raise your kids or take care of your family will always be there, in which case, your confidence in your choices becomes the nailing point. Hormonal changes: Itâ€™s normal for your hormones to change as your baby grows. This change can lead to frequent urination, weak ligaments, and constipation.

Increased pressure: Your uterus expands during pregnancy to give room for your babyâ€™s growth and, in turn, presses the bladder. So, any little pressure, like a sneeze, laugh, or cough, exerts more pressure on the bladder.

Medications: Specific medications contribute to bladder leaks. If youâ€™re taking some medicines, check with your doctor for alternatives.

1.Pelvic Floor Exercises

The pelvic floor supports your uterus, urinary tract, and bladder; strengthening keeps bladder leaks at bay. Aim to do Kegels daily, and you can hold your pelvic floor when you sneeze to avoid placing more pressure on it. However

Maintaining a healthy weight is crucial as your doctor advises to avoid extra strain on your bladder. Your developing baby is already placing a lot of pressure on your bladder, and you can imagine how much worse the pressure will be with additional weight gain.

5.Avoid Bladder Irritants.

Caffeine, carbonated drinks, spicy and acidic foods irritate your bladder, making it difficult to control urination. So, avoid these foods and beverages that cause your bladder leaks from your diet.

Donâ€™t Allow Bladder Leaks to Hold You Back

Prevent Bladder Leaks When Sneezing During Pregnancy

Without a doubt, a leaking bladder when you sneeze during pregnancy is embarrassing and an inconvenience. But the good news is that it clears after giving birth. In the meantime, you can practice these five tips to stop the leaks.

Good rest is vital for a strong and healthy immune system. A tired body wonâ€™t fight off illness like a well-rested one.

Boost Your Immune Today

blog_posts.title: Dysgeusia: Understanding Why Everything Tastes Bad During Pregnancy
blog_posts.content:
Dysgeusia.

Pregnancy is a miraculous journey that brings joy, excitement, and, sometimes, unexpected challenges. One of the challenges that some pregnant women face is Dysgeusia, where everything tastes bad. From your favorite foods to once-craved delicacies, suddenly, flavors become unappetizing or even repulsive. Strange, right?

 

Dysgeusia

The good news is that Dysegeusia is a temporary pregnancy symptom and clears over time. This blog post discusses the reasons behind Dysgeusia and offers helpful tips for navigating it.

1. Hormonal Changes

Your body undergoes significant hormonal changes during pregnancy to support the babyâ€™s development. These hormonal shifts, particularly increased levels of estrogen and progesterone, can change the perception of your taste and smell, leading to a distorted sense of taste. Youâ€™ll start noticing that foods you once enjoyed may now taste overly salty, metallic, or simply unpleasant.

 

2.Heightened Sense of Smell

A heightened sense of smell is a common pregnancy symptom that may also intensify the flavors of foods, making them overwhelming or unappetizing. Once pleasant and even subtle aromas may now trigger feelings of nausea or aversion, making it challenging to enjoy meals.

 

3.Changes in Taste Buds

Thanks to the hormonal changes during your pregnancy, youâ€™ll notice that your taste buds have changed altering the taste of foods. Sweet tastes may become too intense, salty tastes overpowering, and bitter or sour flavors may be particularly unappetizing. This can contribute to overall dissatisfaction with food taste during pregnancy.

 

4.Nausea and Morning Sickness

Morning sickness, which can strike at any time, is a common pregnancy symptom affecting your taste perception. The feeling of nausea, often accompanied by vomiting, can create an aversion to certain foods and flavors, further contributing to the sensation that everything tastes bad. Certain odors or tastes that were once loved can suddenly trigger a strong aversion, making it difficult to find pleasure in previously enjoyed dishes.

 

Tips for Coping with the Taste Changes

 

Try out different flavors: Start experimenting with new flavors to find ones that are more appealing during pregnancy. Spices, herbs, and mild citrus flavors may help with your altered taste perception.

Choose cold or room-temperature foods: Sometimes, food temperature can affect your taste perception. Cold or room-temperature foods may be more tolerable than hot meals, so try experimenting with different temperature ranges.

Stay hydrated: Proper hydration can help reduce the intensity of taste changes. Sipping water throughout the day and staying well-hydrated can also help alleviate some of the unpleasant tastes.

Choose nutrient-dense foods: Focus on selecting nutrient-dense foods that are important for your health and the babyâ€™s development. While taste may be compromised, ensuring a well-balanced diet will help meet nutritional needs during this crucial time.

Talk to your OB/GYN: If taste changes persist or are causing difficulty maintaining a healthy diet, donâ€™t hesitate to reach out to your OB/GYN. They can provide additional guidance and support to help manage this symptom.

 

In Closing

Without a doubt, experiencing Dysgeusia during pregnancy can be frustrating and disheartening. However, understanding the underlying causes and employing the four strategies to navigate this temporary phase can help alleviate the challenges.

Itâ€™s no secret that your baby will come with extra expenses from hospital bills, diapers, formula, and childcare. The secret is ensuring you pay the minimum balance on time for good credit.

First, figure out your babyâ€™s and familyâ€™s budget for the month, and start paying off as much debt as you can with what is left. For example, if 5% of your monthly income goes towards paying off the debt, you can increase it to 10 percent depending on what you can manage as you find other ways to cut down your expenses.

Set Up an Emergency Fund

Despite how financially savvy youâ€™re, you canâ€™t predict the unexpected expenses that creep up when you have a baby. For instance, a trip to the pediatrician in the middle of the night, formula when you donâ€™t produce enough, or the expenses that come with replacing a nanny.

Building an emergency fund provides you with a financial safety net. It will keep you from borrowing money and increasing your debt because of unexpected expenses. Aim to save up a fund that can cover your living expenses for six to nine months.

With all the physical and emotional stress that comes with having a baby, you wonâ€™t have the time and energy to worry about money and be counting every shilling all the time. Creating a budget ensures youâ€™re financially prepared when your baby arrives.

While you might be tempted to go on a shopping spree buying all that you think will make your life easier, your baby doesnâ€™t require so much. A budget will help you estimate the necessary baby needs like formula and diapers and set aside funds without going over what you can afford.

Cost. One key factor that should guide your choice of a nanny is the cost implications. A day nanny is cheaper as you only pay for the hours worked. On the other hand, a live-in nanny is expensive since you need to pay more and still foot the bills for their accommodation and feeding expenses.

Age of the child. When deciding whether to hire a live-in nanny or a day nanny, you might want to consider how old the baby is. Consistency. Consistency is essential in your childâ€™s growth. A live-in nanny offers more consistency in childcare than the on-and-off services your child gets from a day nanny.

Privacy and space. One of the reasons a live-in nanny might not be a suitable option is the need for privacy and personal space. If your family prioritizes privacy and family moments, then a day nanny will do.

Risks and Benefits of Caffeine during Pregnancy

Caffeine is well known for its stimulating nature and consequent addiction when consumed for a long time. Some pregnant mothers consume caffeine following an addiction, while others get a craving for the first time. Craving during pregnancy is always a heated topic, and in most scenarios, the items craved are weird and can even be harmful to oneâ€™s health. As your body transitions through the different phases, a need for more specific nutrients and vitamins increases. In the same way, it is common for pregnant women to crave beverages rich in caffeine in response to the demand for extra energy and stimulation. It is, however, imperative to weigh the good or bad you are doing to your body and your unborn baby when you heed those random cravings.

Risks and Benefits of Caffeine during Pregnancy

Sources of Caffeine

The best way to keep your diet in check is by acquainting yourself with the ingredients and chemical content in everything you consume. The knowledge is good, especially when you want to maximize or stop consumption of specific foods or drinks. Caffeine, in our case, is commonly present in beverages such as coffee, tea, chocolate, energy drinks, and some soft drinks. Some over-the-counter prescriptions may also contain a considerable amount of caffeine.

 

Benefits of Caffeine during Pregnancy

Pre-pregnancy, caffeine consumption is natural. It provides the stimulation needed to maintain alertness and keep your body awake. Due to the weariness and fatigue that comes with pregnancy, taking tea or coffee in moderation may be helpful. It also helps with gestational diabetes. It requires discipline to escape the habit and not end up in addiction, with the recommended amount of caffeine being 200mg per day.

 

Why You Should Cut Down Your Consumption of Caffeinated Drinks

Caffeine intake during pregnancy can cause serious threats to your health and that of your baby. The most common effects are low birth weight, stillbirth, and miscarriage. It also increases the urge to urinate frequently, which may cause bladder irritation and a consequent risk of dehydration. Given its stimulating nature, studies have shown characteristics of restlessness in women and babies exposed to excessive caffeine intake. It interrupts sleep patterns and may cause sleeping disorders. Caffeine also interferes with the heartbeat rate and may even hinder normal growth in babies.

 

How to Take Control of Your Caffeine Intake

Your health and your unborn baby should be your number one priority. However strong the urge for that sip of coffee, you do not always have to give in. You can adopt other alternatives to help cut down on caffeine and maintain a healthy pregnancy, such as taking juices and decaffeinated coffee or tea, avoiding energy drinks at all costs, seeking guidance from your pharmacists on caffeine-free medication, and taking enough water.

 

The health threats associated with caffeine intake during pregnancy outweigh its benefits. It is, therefore, healthy to shun the consumption of such drinks that expose you and your baby to such dangers for a healthy pregnancy.

The noises and other external disruptions could be the cause of why your baby finds it hard to fall asleep or keeps waking up from time to time. blog_posts.title: Why Cryptic Pregnancy Usually Goes unnoticed
blog_posts.content:
Pregnancy is typically an exciting and well-recognized event. Still, there are rare cases when a woman may experience a cryptic pregnancy, which goes unnoticed until the later stages or even until delivery.

What is a cryptic pregnancy?

A cryptic pregnancy (or stealth pregnancy) is when a pregnant person doesnâ€™t know theyâ€™re pregnant. In some cases, a person may only realize theyâ€™re pregnant because labor begins.

Most people realize theyâ€™re pregnant somewhere between four and 12 weeks of pregnancy. This could be because they have symptoms of pregnancy or because they missed their period. A positive result on a pregnancy test can confirm pregnancy. With a cryptic pregnancy, nothing triggers a person to believe theyâ€™re pregnant. This could be because they donâ€™t have symptoms of pregnancy or mistake symptoms of pregnancy as a virus, or their pregnancy test result was wrong.

This blog post delves into the intriguing world of cryptic pregnancies and why they usually go unnoticed.

Biological Factors

Cryptic or stealth pregnancies occur due to a combination of biological factors. The hormonal changes accompanying pregnancy may not be as pronounced in some women, leading to the absence or irregularity of typical pregnancy symptoms.

Additionally, factors such as low body weight, irregular menstrual cycles, and anatomical variations can further complicate the recognition of pregnancy. These biological factors make it challenging for women and healthcare providers to identify the presence of a growing fetus.

Psychological Factors

The mind is a powerful influencer, and psychological factors play a significant role in detecting a cryptic pregnancy. Sometimes, women may experience denial or disbelief regarding their pregnancy, leading them to overlook or downplay the physical signs.

Psychological stress, trauma, or a lack of prenatal care may contribute to this phenomenon. Not forgetting societal and cultural influences, fear of judgment, or personal circumstances can influence a womanâ€™s perception and acknowledgement of her pregnancy, causing it to remain concealed.

Misinterpretation of Symptoms

Many symptoms associated with pregnancy can also mimic other health conditions or be attributed to lifestyle factors. Women experiencing cryptic pregnancies may mistake signs like weight gain, fatigue, or changes in appetite for other reasons, such as stress, hormonal imbalances, or irregularities in their menstrual cycle.

This misinterpretation of symptoms can lead to the assumption that they are not pregnant, causing the pregnancy to remain undetected.

Lack of Routine Prenatal Care

Prenatal care is crucial in monitoring and detecting pregnancies, but women experiencing cryptic pregnancies forego or delay seeking prenatal care. The absence of routine check-ups and ultrasound examinations, typically part of prenatal care, significantly increases the likelihood of an unnoticed pregnancy. Without these regular appointments, healthcare professionals miss vital opportunities to identify the growing fetus and educate women about their pregnancy.

5. False Negative Test

Though false negative tests in pregnancy are rare, they can happen if you take them improperly or too early. As a result, you will believe youâ€™re not pregnant, while in reality, you are. Another contributor is low HCG levels, which are responsible for pregnancy symptoms. You wouldnâ€™t consider taking a pregnancy test if you have no signs.

6. Small Baby Bump

Sometimes your baby bump may not be visible depending on your babyâ€™s weight, growth rate and position in the womb. A small baby bump is often common among first-time younger women since their abdominal muscles are still tight. It is also the case with overweight women, where the extra weight hides the bump.

blog_posts.title: Addressing Speech Delay in Kids and the Various Non-Medical Contributing Factors
blog_posts.content:
Speech delay in kids has been a major concern for most parents. While it is normal for some kids to develop speech earlier than other kids their age, the delay in some becomes worrisome, with parents seeking answers as to why. Besides the medical factors, there exists an array of non-medical factors that contribute to delay in speech development. Understanding the contributing factors is essential for early identification of the crises to facilitate necessary intervention to address delays in speech formation. Below are some of the non-medical factors and the possible mitigating actions.

Environmental Factors

The environment in which a child grows plays a significant role in determining how soon they develop speech. For instance, children born in homes where communication is done using different languages or grow up in areas with loud noises may have a hard time in speech development

Family interactions

Kids look up to the older members of the family as models for the most part of their growing up. Through direct interactions, they can mimic speech patterns and language intricacies. In families where vocal interactions are limited or lack in entirety, children become victims of delayed speech. Narrations and conversations in a family setup give room for nurturing the communicative abilities of the kid.

Excessive Screen Time

In the current era, where digital learning and entertainment are idolized, the impact of excessive screen time on kids has been overlooked. Some parents want to keep their kids entertained and learning, while others use screen time as a distraction for their kids as they carry out other errands, which is understandable. Regardless of the many benefits, however, the passive nature of these screen entertainments or learning sessions does not promote active speaking, thus hindering speech development in the long run.

Social and Emotional Factors

Kids who have difficulties interacting with others or are shy rarely engage in active speaking, which may limit their chance at speech development. Also, kids who grow up in an indoor setup have limited exposure and find it difficult to open up to the outside life. Likewise, kids with anxiety disorders or who have had traumatic experiences have difficulties communicating.

Tips to help with speech development in kids

While it is advisable to seek medical intervention when you note a delay in the speech development of your kid, below are some practical home remedies to help improve the situation.

 

Create an enabling environment that encourages active communication

Read books together to help build on words and vocabulary

Encourage imitation

Provide opportunities for social interactions

Use Visual Aids as well as monitored screen time for interactive speech training resources

Practice patience and understanding

There are a myriad of non-medical factors that can lead to speech delay in kids. While some cases of speech delay require professional intervention, it is possible to handle the situation by application of home remedies such as interactive reading sessions, encouraging imitation, use of visual aids, interactive talking with patience, and understanding of your childâ€™s needs.

The Fluid is Clear and Odorless

Youâ€™ll experience a popping sound or pressure when your water breaks. Itâ€™s usually painless but the leakage increases in frequency.
